description:
In this engaging episode of 3ABN Today Bible Q&A, Pastor James Rafferty and Shelley Quinn join host Ricky Carter to unpack some of Scripture’s most thought-provoking questions. Topics include the seven demons in Luke 8, challenging passages like Judges 11 and Psalm 58, the meaning of the Second Coming, and end-time insights from Genesis 49. The panel also addresses practical and heartfelt questions on rebaptism, remarriage, Heaven, and why sin is traced through Adam. Join us for clear, biblical answers that deepen understanding and strengthen your walk with Christ.



Send us your Bible Questions! 
By email: BibleQA@3abn.org




1. Luke chapter 8 says seven demons were cast out of Mary. Who or what were those demons?What were the seven demons cast out of Mary in Luke 8?

2. Can you please explain Judges 11:34-40?  

3. Why do people always refer to the coming of God’s return as the second coming of Christ? Why is it called the Second Coming of Christ?

4. What does Genesis 49:2-27 mean for the tribes in the last days? 

5. Are there sins that would require a baptized Christian to be rebaptized? Are there sins that require rebaptism?

6. Can you please explain Psalm 58:3? Is this verse saying children are born wicked from the womb?
 
7. How can we live in Heaven if we are constantly reminded of the sins that put the nail prints in Jesus' hands? How can we live in Heaven remembering the sins that crucified Jesus?

8.  I've heard that if a person is divorced and has remarried, they are still living in adultery, even though they have asked God to forgive them. Is this true? Is remarriage after divorce considered adultery?

9. Romans 5:12 says, "Therefore, just as through one man sin entered the world, and death through sin, and thus death spread to all men, because all sinned." Paul explains that sin entered the world through one man, Adam, and salvation comes through one man, Jesus. But wasn't it  Eve who fell in the Garden of Eden? Why does Paul say sin entered the world through Adam?  Why does sin enter through Adam if Eve sinned first?
